q: A new steel tyre is fitted on a wheel centre in the wheel shop of a workshop by:

options.A: Pressing the cold tyre over the wheel centre by hydraulic pressure alone
options.B: Heating the tyre so that it expands, placing it over the wheel centre and allowing it to cool and contract into a tight shrink fit
options.C: Welding the tyre to the wheel centre all round
options.D: Bolting the tyre to the wheel centre

e: The tyre is heated so that it expands, placed over the wheel centre, and on cooling it contracts into a tight shrink fit on the wheel centre.

q: The economic batch quantity in batch manufacture in a workshop is fixed so as to balance:

options.A: The material cost and the labour cost of the batch
options.B: The fixed cost and the variable cost of the workshop
options.C: The setting-up (preparation) cost of the batch and the cost of carrying or holding the stock produced
options.D: The cost of inspection and the cost of transport of the batch

e: The economic batch quantity is fixed so as to balance the setting-up (preparation) cost of the batch against the cost of carrying or holding the stock produced.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Provision for new rolling stock is made under Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock.
2. Provision for workshop machinery and plant is made under Plan Head 41 - Machinery and Plant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: provision for new rolling stock is made under Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock, and for workshop machinery and plant under Plan Head 41 - Machinery and Plant.

q: Which of the following is included in the definition of 'manufacturing process' under the Factories Act, 1948?

options.A: Cultivation of crops on land within the factory premises
options.C: Running a canteen for the workers of the factory
options.D: Maintenance of the accounts and records of the factory

e: Generating, transforming or transmitting power is expressly included in the definition of 'manufacturing process' under the Factories Act, 1948.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a child who has not completed his fourteenth year:

options.A: Shall not be required or allowed to work in any factory
options.B: May be employed in non-hazardous processes with a certificate of fitness
options.C: May be employed for not more than four and a half hours in a day
options.D: May be employed with the written consent of his parents

e: A child who has not completed his fourteenth year shall not be required or allowed to work in any factory at all.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, every hoist and lift in a factory must be thoroughly examined by a competent person at intervals not exceeding:
e: Every hoist and lift in a factory must be thoroughly examined by a competent person at intervals not exceeding six months.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, spittoons in a factory are required to be:

options.A: Provided only near the latrines and urinals
options.B: Provided only in the canteen and rest rooms
options.C: Provided in sufficient numbers at convenient places and maintained in a clean and hygienic condition
options.D: Provided only where more than 500 workers are employed

e: Spittoons are required to be provided in sufficient numbers at convenient places in the factory and maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.

q: Where a manufacturing process in a factory involves risk of injury to the eyes of the persons employed, from particles or fragments thrown off or from excessive light, the Factories Act, 1948 requires that:

options.A: Effective screens or suitable goggles shall be provided for the protection of the persons employed
options.B: A special risk allowance shall be paid to the persons employed
options.C: Such a process shall be prohibited altogether in the factory
options.D: The persons employed shall be examined by a doctor every month

e: Where a process involves risk of injury to the eyes from particles or fragments thrown off or from excessive light, effective screens or suitable goggles shall be provided for the protection of the persons employed.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a fine can be imposed on a worker only:

options.A: For any act or omission of which the employer disapproves
options.B: Where the worker gives his consent in writing
options.C: For acts specified by the Inspector of Factories without any notice
options.D: For an act or omission specified in a notice which has been approved by the prescribed authority and is displayed at the prescribed place in the establishment

e: A fine can be imposed only for an act or omission specified in a notice which has been approved by the prescribed authority and is displayed at the prescribed place in the establishment.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a deduction from the wages of a worker on account of damage to, or loss of, goods expressly entrusted to his custody cannot exceed:

options.A: Fifty per cent of the wages of the worker for the wage period
options.B: The amount of the damage or loss actually caused to the employer by his neglect or default
options.C: Three per cent of the wages of the worker for the wage period
options.D: The wages of the worker for one month

e: A deduction on account of damage or loss cannot exceed the amount of the damage or loss actually caused to the employer by the worker's neglect or default.

q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, an employer is not liable to pay compensation in respect of an injury which:

options.A: Results in the death of the workman
options.B: Is caused by an accident arising out of and in the course of the employment
options.C: Does not result in total or partial disablement of the workman for a period exceeding three days
options.D: Is reported to the employer after three days of its occurrence

e: The employer is not liable to pay compensation where the injury does not result in total or partial disablement of the workman for a period exceeding three days.

q: An employee is covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 if his monthly wages do not exceed:
e: An employee is covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 if his monthly wages do not exceed Rs 21,000.

q: The Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act provides:

options.A: An assurance benefit, linked to the member's provident fund, payable to his family or nominee if he dies while in service
options.B: A monthly pension to the member after his superannuation
options.C: Free medical treatment to the member and his family
options.D: A loan to the member for the marriage of his children or for housing

e: The EDLI Scheme provides an assurance benefit, linked to the member's provident fund, payable to his family or nominee if he dies while in service.

q: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the bonus payable to employees for an accounting year must ordinarily be paid in cash within:

options.A: Three months of the close of the accounting year
options.B: Eight months of the close of the accounting year
options.C: Six months of the close of the accounting year
options.D: Twelve months of the close of the accounting year

e: The bonus payable for an accounting year must ordinarily be paid in cash within eight months of the close of the accounting year.

q: For an establishment other than a banking company, the 'allocable surplus' under the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 is:

options.A: 50 per cent of the available surplus
options.B: 67 per cent of the available surplus
options.C: 60 per cent of the available surplus
options.D: 75 per cent of the available surplus

e: For an establishment other than a banking company, the allocable surplus under the Payment of Bonus Act is 60 per cent of the available surplus.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 shall be paid within thirty days from the date on which it becomes payable.
2. The condition of five years' continuous service applies in every case, including where the service is terminated on account of the death or disablement of the employee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: gratuity shall be paid within thirty days from the date it becomes payable. Statement 2 is wrong, as the five-year service condition does not apply in cases of death or disablement.

q: The gratuity payable to an employee may be forfeited, wholly or in part, where:

options.A: The employee resigns after completing ten years of service
options.B: His services are terminated for riotous or disorderly conduct, or for an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of his employment
options.C: The employee is transferred to another workshop
options.D: The employee's services are terminated on his attaining the age of superannuation

e: Gratuity may be forfeited, wholly or in part, where the services are terminated for riotous or disorderly conduct, or for an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of employment.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lay-off compensation payable to a workman under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 is equal to fifty per cent of the total of his basic wages and dearness allowance.
2. Lay-off compensation is payable only to a workman who has completed not less than one year of continuous service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: lay-off compensation equals fifty per cent of the total of basic wages and dearness allowance, and it is payable only to a workman who has completed not less than one year of continuous service.

q: A workman who has completed one year of continuous service cannot be retrenched unless he is given one month's notice or wages in lieu thereof and, in addition, compensation equivalent to:

options.A: 15 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service
options.B: 7 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service
options.C: 21 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service
options.D: 30 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service

e: A retrenched workman with one year of continuous service must be given one month's notice or wages in lieu, plus compensation equal to 15 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service.

q: Which of the following is NOT 'retrenchment' within the meaning of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947?

options.A: Termination of the services of surplus staff rendered redundant by rationalisation
options.B: Termination of the services of a workman on abolition of the post held by him
options.C: Termination of the services of a workman due to shortage of work or material in the establishment
options.D: Termination of the services of a workman on his attaining the age of superannuation

e: Termination of service on attaining the age of superannuation is expressly excluded from the definition of retrenchment under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

q: A Grievance Redressal Committee is required to be set up under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 in an industrial establishment employing:
e: A Grievance Redressal Committee is required to be set up in an industrial establishment employing 20 or more workmen.

q: An application for the registration of a Trade Union under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 must be made by at least:
e: An application for registration of a trade union under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 must be made by at least seven members of the union.

q: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 applies to an establishment in which the number of workmen employed as contract labour on any day of the preceding twelve months is:
e: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 applies to an establishment in which 20 or more workmen are employed as contract labour on any day of the preceding twelve months.

q: If a contractor fails to make payment of wages to contract labour within the prescribed period, the liability to make the payment falls, in the first instance, on:

options.A: The licensing authority under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act
options.C: The workmen, who must await payment by the contractor
options.D: The principal employer, who may recover the amount so paid from the contractor

e: If the contractor fails to pay wages within the prescribed period, the principal employer must make the payment and may recover the amount so paid from the contractor.

q: The minimum rates of wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 must be reviewed by the appropriate Government at intervals not exceeding:
e: The minimum rates of wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 must be reviewed by the appropriate Government at intervals not exceeding five years.

q: The allowed time for a job is 40 hours and a worker completes it in 32 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 60. Under the Halsey premium bonus plan (bonus at 50 per cent of the value of the time saved), the bonus payable to him for the job is:
e: Time saved = 40 - 32 = 8 hours; Halsey bonus = 50 per cent of the value of time saved = 0.5 x 8 x 60 = Rs 240.

q: The allowed time for a job is 24 hours and a worker completes it in 18 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 50. Under the Rowan premium bonus plan, his total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus) are:
e: Rowan plan: time wages = 18 x 50 = Rs 900; bonus = (time saved / allowed time) x time wages = (6 / 24) x 900 = Rs 225; total earnings = Rs 1,125.

q: Under the CLW pattern incentive scheme, the allowed time for a job is 12 hours, a worker completes it in 9 hours and his hourly rate of wages is Rs 60. His total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus for the full time saved) are:
e: Under the CLW pattern, bonus is paid for the full time saved: wages for time taken 9 x 60 = Rs 540 plus bonus 3 x 60 = Rs 180, giving total earnings of Rs 720.

q: Under the Bedaux point system, the standard output for a job is fixed at 480 points (B units), representing 8 standard hours of work. A worker completes the job in 6 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 50 and the bonus payable is 75 per cent of the value of the points saved. His total earnings for the job are:
e: Points saved = 480 - (6 x 60) = 120 points, worth 120 x (50/60) = Rs 100; bonus = 75 per cent of 100 = Rs 75; total earnings = time wages Rs 300 + Rs 75 = Rs 375.

q: The allowed time for a job is 20 hours and a worker completes it in 25 hours. The efficiency of the worker for the job is:
e: Efficiency = allowed time / time taken x 100 = 20 / 25 x 100 = 80 per cent; taking more time than allowed gives an efficiency below 100 per cent.

q: The opening balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of a workshop is Rs 12,00,000. During the year, labour, material and on-cost of Rs 48,00,000 are booked to jobs, and outturn of Rs 52,00,000 is transferred out. The closing balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + cost booked - outturn transferred out = 12,00,000 + 48,00,000 - 52,00,000 = Rs 8,00,000.

q: The total cost of Periodic Overhaul of 60 coaches in a workshop during a period is Rs 1,20,00,000. The average cost of Periodic Overhaul per coach is:
e: Average cost of periodic overhaul per coach = 1,20,00,000 / 60 = Rs 2,00,000.

q: In a workshop foundry, 500 tonnes of metal were melted and charged into the cupola during a period, and the weight of good castings produced was 400 tonnes. The yield of the foundry for the period is:
e: Foundry yield = weight of good castings / metal charged x 100 = 400 / 500 x 100 = 80 per cent.

q: The standing (fixed) charges of a machine shop for a period are Rs 1,20,000 and the effective machine hours worked are 4,000. The running charges of the machines average Rs 15 per machine hour. The machine-hour rate of the shop is:
e: Machine-hour rate = standing charges per machine hour (1,20,000 / 4,000 = Rs 30) plus running charges of Rs 15 = Rs 45 per machine hour.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop for a period is Rs 2,40,000 and the direct wages booked to jobs in the shop during the same period are Rs 6,00,000. The shop on-cost rate, as a percentage of direct wages, is:
e: Shop on-cost rate = 2,40,000 / 6,00,000 x 100 = 40 per cent of direct wages.

q: On-cost absorbed (recovered) on jobs during a period at the predetermined rate is Rs 60,000, while the actual on-cost incurred in the period is Rs 55,000. The position in respect of absorption of on-cost is:
e: On-cost absorbed (Rs 60,000) exceeds the actual on-cost incurred (Rs 55,000), so the on-cost is over-absorbed by Rs 5,000.

q: On a workshop job, material of Rs 60,000 and labour of Rs 35,000 are booked, shop on-cost charged on it is Rs 7,000 and proforma on-cost applicable to the job is Rs 4,000. The total (full) cost of the job is:
e: Total (full) cost = material 60,000 + labour 35,000 + shop on-cost 7,000 + proforma on-cost 4,000 = Rs 1,06,000.

q: On a workshop job, direct material of Rs 1,10,000, direct labour of Rs 60,000 and direct expenses of Rs 15,000 are booked. The prime cost of the job is:
e: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses = 1,10,000 + 60,000 + 15,000 = Rs 1,85,000.

q: The total cost of a shop for a period is Rs 9,00,000 and the standard hours of work produced in the period are 15,000. The cost per standard hour is:
e: Cost per standard hour = total cost of the shop / standard hours produced = 9,00,000 / 15,000 = Rs 60.

q: A workshop employee, whose last drawn monthly wages were Rs 23,400, retires after completing 30 years of service. His gratuity, at 15 days' wages for every completed year of service (15/26 of the monthly wages for each year), is:
e: Gratuity = 15/26 x monthly wages x completed years of service = (15/26) x 23,400 x 30 = Rs 4,05,000.

q: The allowed (standard) time for manufacturing one component in a workshop is 30 minutes. During a period, 1,000 such components are produced. The standard hours earned for the outturn are:
e: Standard hours earned = 1,000 components x 30 minutes = 30,000 minutes = 500 standard hours.

q: The machining operation of 'turning', by which external cylindrical surfaces are produced on a rotating workpiece, is performed on:
e: Turning, by which external cylindrical surfaces are produced on a rotating workpiece, is performed on a lathe machine.

q: A milling machine in a workshop produces flat and profiled surfaces by means of:
e: A milling machine produces flat and profiled surfaces by means of a rotating multi-point cutter.

q: A planing machine differs from a shaping machine in that, in a planing machine:

options.A: The workpiece reciprocates past a stationary cutting tool
options.B: The cutting tool reciprocates over a stationary workpiece
options.C: The cutter rotates continuously at high speed
options.D: The workpiece is rotated in a chuck

e: In a planing machine the workpiece reciprocates past a stationary cutting tool, whereas in a shaping machine the tool reciprocates over a stationary workpiece.

q: In machining terminology, the operation of 'boring' means:

options.A: Making a fresh hole in solid metal with a drill
options.B: Cutting an internal screw thread in a hole
options.C: Chamfering the mouth of a hole
options.D: Enlarging and finishing a hole that has already been drilled

e: Boring means enlarging and finishing a hole that has already been drilled; it does not make a fresh hole in solid metal.

q: 'Reaming' is carried out on a drilled hole in a workshop in order to:

options.B: Finish the hole to an accurate size and a smooth surface
options.C: Cut internal threads in the hole

e: Reaming is carried out on a drilled hole to finish it to an accurate size and a smooth surface.

q: An internal screw thread in a hole is cut in a workshop with the help of a hand tool called a:
e: An internal screw thread in a hole is cut with a tap; a die is used for external threads.

q: A vernier caliper, as used in a workshop, is an instrument for measuring:

options.A: Internal and external dimensions and the depth of a job
options.B: The speed of rotation of a shaft

e: A vernier caliper is an instrument for measuring internal and external dimensions and the depth of a job.

q: Measuring instruments and gauges used in a workshop are subjected to periodic calibration primarily in order to:

options.D: Ensure that their accuracy is maintained against standard references

e: Periodic calibration ensures that the accuracy of measuring instruments and gauges is maintained against standard references, so that measurements remain reliable.

q: Case hardening, as a surface-hardening process, is ordinarily applied to components made of:

options.C: Low-carbon (mild) steel, so that the surface hardens while the core remains tough

e: Case hardening is ordinarily applied to low-carbon (mild) steel, so that the surface can be hardened while the core remains soft and tough.

q: In the heat treatment of steel in a workshop, 'quenching' means:

options.A: Slow cooling of the heated component in the furnace
options.B: Rapid cooling of the heated component in water or oil
options.C: Reheating the component to a low temperature
options.D: Heating the component without any cooling

e: Quenching means rapid cooling of the heated steel component in water or oil, which hardens the steel.

q: 'Forging' of a metal component in a smithy consists of:

options.A: Shaping the heated metal by hammering or pressing
options.B: Melting the metal and pouring it into a mould
options.C: Joining two pieces of metal by fusion
options.D: Cutting the metal on a lathe

e: Forging consists of shaping the heated metal by hammering or pressing; the metal is not melted as in casting.

q: The cupola in a workshop foundry is a furnace used for:

options.D: Melting cast iron for producing castings

e: The cupola in a workshop foundry is a furnace used for melting cast iron for producing castings.

q: A casting defect known as 'misrun' occurs when:

options.A: Gas is trapped in the casting, producing holes in it
options.C: The molten metal fails to fill the mould cavity completely before solidifying
options.D: Sand from the mould gets mixed with the metal of the casting

e: A misrun occurs when the molten metal fails to fill the mould cavity completely before solidifying, leaving the casting incomplete.

q: The 'machining allowance' provided on a pattern/casting means:

options.A: The taper given to the pattern for its easy withdrawal from the mould
options.B: The extra material left on the casting to be removed by machining to the finished size
options.C: The shrinkage of the metal on cooling
options.D: The clearance between the pattern and the moulding box

e: Machining allowance is the extra material left on the casting, over the finished size, to be removed by machining to reach the final dimensions.

q: In a sand mould, the 'riser' serves the purpose of:

options.A: Feeding liquid metal to the casting to make up for shrinkage as it solidifies
options.B: Letting out the gases formed in the mould
options.C: Supporting the core in position in the mould
options.D: Filtering the molten metal before it enters the mould cavity

e: The riser serves as a reservoir that feeds liquid metal to the casting to make up for shrinkage as the metal solidifies.

q: Brazing differs from soldering in that, in brazing:

options.A: No filler metal is used for joining
options.B: The parts are joined without any heating
options.C: The joint produced is weaker than a soldered joint
options.D: The filler metal used melts at a much higher temperature than the solder used in soldering

e: Brazing differs from soldering in that the filler metal used in brazing melts at a much higher temperature than the solder used in soldering, giving a stronger joint.

q: In electric arc welding, the flux coating provided on the electrode serves mainly to:

options.A: Increase the melting point of the electrode
options.B: Cool the weld rapidly after welding
options.C: Form a protective gas shield and slag covering over the molten metal, preventing atmospheric contamination
options.D: Colour the welded joint for identification

e: The flux coating on the electrode forms a protective gas shield and slag covering over the molten metal, preventing atmospheric contamination of the weld.

q: Worn wheel tyres of rolling stock are re-profiled (turned back to the correct profile) in a workshop on a machine known as the:
e: Worn wheel tyres of rolling stock are re-profiled (turned back to the correct profile) on a wheel lathe in the workshop.

q: In a carriage workshop, the operation of 'lifting' a coach means:

options.A: Raising the coach on jacks for under-gear examination in a depot
options.B: Loading the coach on a road trailer for transport
options.C: Increasing the carrying capacity of the coach
options.D: Raising the coach body clear of its bogies so that the body and the bogies can be attended to separately

e: Lifting a coach means raising the coach body clear of its bogies so that the body and the bogies can be attended to separately.

q: In connection with rolling stock in Indian Railways, the abbreviation CBC stands for:
e: In connection with rolling stock in Indian Railways, CBC stands for Centre Buffer Coupler.

q: CAMTECH (Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology), located at Gwalior, is primarily concerned with:

options.C: Development and dissemination of improved maintenance practices and technology for rolling stock and fixed assets

e: CAMTECH (Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology) at Gwalior is primarily concerned with development and dissemination of improved maintenance practices and technology for rolling stock and fixed assets.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical Engineering (IRIMEE), which imparts training to mechanical engineering probationers and supervisors, is located at:
e: The Indian Railways Institute of Mechanical Engineering (IRIMEE), which trains mechanical engineering probationers and supervisors, is located at Jamalpur.

q: The workshop at Guntapalli (near Vijayawada) of South Central Railway is primarily engaged in:

options.D: Repair and periodic overhaul of wagons

e: The workshop at Guntapalli (near Vijayawada) of South Central Railway is primarily engaged in repair and periodic overhaul of wagons.

q: The railway workshop at Jhansi (North Central Railway) is primarily a:
e: The railway workshop at Jhansi (North Central Railway) is primarily a wagon repair workshop.

q: The railway workshop at Ajmer (North Western Railway) is a composite workshop which undertakes:

options.C: Periodic overhaul and repairs of locomotives, coaches and wagons

e: The Ajmer workshop (North Western Railway) is a composite workshop which undertakes periodic overhaul and repairs of locomotives, coaches and wagons.

q: At the Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka, the wheels for rolling stock are produced by the process of:
e: At the Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka, the wheels for rolling stock are produced by the process of steel casting.

q: In production control in a workshop, 'scheduling' of jobs means:

options.A: Deciding the sequence of shops through which a job will pass
options.B: Following up the progress of jobs in the shops
options.C: Loading the machines of a shop to their full capacity
options.D: Fixing the dates or times by which the successive operations on a job are to be started and completed

e: In production control, scheduling means fixing the dates or times by which the successive operations on a job are to be started and completed.

q: Rolling stock which has been surveyed and condemned in a workshop is finally disposed of:

options.A: Through the Stores department, ordinarily by sale through public auction
options.B: By the workshop itself to local scrap dealers without any auction
options.C: By free issue to other workshops for their use
options.D: By dumping it in the workshop yard itself

e: Rolling stock surveyed and condemned in a workshop is finally disposed of through the Stores department, ordinarily by sale through public auction.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Workshop Accounts Office exercises internal check over the expenditure incurred in the workshop.
2. The statutory audit of the accounts of a railway workshop is conducted by the Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Workshop Accounts Office exercises internal check over workshop expenditure, and the statutory audit is conducted by the Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: Under the Halsey-Weir premium bonus plan, the allowed time for a job is 24 hours and a worker completes it in 18 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 40. His total earnings for the job are:
e: Halsey-Weir plan: time wages = 18 x 40 = Rs 720; bonus = one-third of the value of time saved = (1/3) x 6 x 40 = Rs 80; total earnings = Rs 800.

q: Under Taylor's differential piece-rate system, the standard output for a day is fixed at 100 units and the ordinary piece rate is Rs 4 per unit. A worker produces 90 units in the day. His earnings for the day are (rate for below-standard output being 80 per cent of the ordinary piece rate):
e: Output of 90 units is below the standard of 100 units, so the lower differential rate of 80 per cent of Rs 4 = Rs 3.20 per unit applies; earnings = 90 x 3.20 = Rs 288.

q: Under Merrick's multiple piece-rate system, the standard output for a job is 200 units and the ordinary piece rate is Rs 2.50 per unit. A worker produces 230 units, his efficiency being above 100 per cent of the standard, for which the rate payable is 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate. His earnings are:
e: Efficiency above 100 per cent earns 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate: 2.50 x 1.20 = Rs 3.00 per unit; earnings = 230 x 3.00 = Rs 690.

q: Under Emerson's efficiency (premium bonus) plan, a worker attains exactly 100 per cent efficiency on a job. His time wages for the job are Rs 4,000 and the bonus payable at 100 per cent efficiency is 20 per cent of the time wages. His total earnings for the job are:
e: At 100 per cent efficiency under Emerson's plan the bonus is 20 per cent of time wages: total earnings = 4,000 + 0.20 x 4,000 = Rs 4,800.

q: A workshop worker is engaged on piece work with a guaranteed minimum day wage of Rs 1,600. During a day he produces 280 units at a piece rate of Rs 5 per unit. The wages payable to him for the day are:
e: Piece earnings = 280 x 5 = Rs 1,400, which is below the guaranteed minimum day wage of Rs 1,600, so the worker is paid Rs 1,600 for the day.

q: During a year, 80 workers left a workshop and 100 fresh workers were engaged in their place and for additional posts. The average number of workers on the rolls during the year was 1,500. The labour turnover rate by the flux method is:
e: Flux method: labour turnover = (workers left + workers engaged) / average number of workers x 100 = (80 + 100) / 1,500 x 100 = 12 per cent.

q: A batch of 800 standard components is manufactured in a workshop. The setting-up cost of the machines for the batch is Rs 4,000 and the running cost (material, labour and on-cost) works out to Rs 45 per component. The cost per component of the batch is:
e: Cost per component = running cost per component + setting-up cost per component = 45 + (4,000 / 800) = 45 + 5 = Rs 50.

q: On a workshop job, direct material of Rs 80,000 and direct labour of Rs 50,000 are booked and shop on-cost charged is Rs 20,000. General on-cost is leviable at 10 per cent of the works cost. The total cost of the job, excluding proforma on-cost, is:
e: Works cost = 80,000 + 50,000 + 20,000 = Rs 1,50,000; general on-cost = 10 per cent of works cost = Rs 15,000; total cost = 1,50,000 + 15,000 = Rs 1,65,000.

q: The standard cost of a workshop job was fixed at Rs 52,000. On completion, the actual cost of the job is found to be Rs 55,500. The cost variance on the job is:
e: Actual cost (Rs 55,500) exceeds the standard cost (Rs 52,000) by Rs 3,500, so the cost variance on the job is Rs 3,500 adverse.

q: A machine in a workshop cost Rs 5,00,000. Depreciation on it is charged at 10 per cent per annum on the written down value method. The depreciation chargeable in the second year of its life is:
e: On the written down value method, first-year depreciation = 10 per cent of 5,00,000 = Rs 50,000, leaving Rs 4,50,000; second-year depreciation = 10 per cent of 4,50,000 = Rs 45,000.

q: In a workshop foundry, 800 tonnes of metal were charged into the cupola during a period. The weight of good castings produced was 600 tonnes and the runners, risers and other process returns fit for re-melting weighed 120 tonnes. The melting loss during the period was:
e: Melting loss = metal charged - good castings - process returns fit for re-melting = 800 - 600 - 120 = 80 tonnes.

q: In machining, the operation of 'drilling' consists of:

options.A: Producing a cylindrical hole in a workpiece by means of a rotating multi-point cutting tool called a drill
options.B: Enlarging a previously drilled hole to an accurate size with a single-point tool
options.C: Finishing a drilled hole with a fluted reamer
options.D: Cutting an internal screw thread in a hole

e: Drilling consists of producing a cylindrical hole in a workpiece by means of a rotating multi-point cutting tool called a drill.

q: A slotting machine in a workshop is used mainly for:

options.A: Producing flat surfaces on very large workpieces
options.B: Turning long cylindrical shafts between centres
options.C: Grinding the flanks of gear teeth
options.D: Cutting slots and internal or external keyways by means of a reciprocating ram carrying a single-point tool

e: A slotting machine is used mainly for cutting slots and internal or external keyways by means of a reciprocating ram carrying a single-point tool.

q: In workshop practice, a 'broach' is:

options.A: A multi-toothed cutting tool which is pushed or pulled across a surface or through a hole to machine keyways, splines and profiles
options.B: A hand tool used for scraping bearing surfaces
options.C: A device for holding a workpiece on a milling machine
options.D: An abrasive wheel used for sharpening drills

e: A broach is a multi-toothed cutting tool which is pushed or pulled across a surface or through a hole to machine keyways, splines and profiles.

q: 'Honing' of a component in a workshop is carried out in order to:

options.A: Produce a screw thread on the outside of a cylindrical part
options.B: Remove the scale formed on a forging
options.C: Harden the surface of a gear tooth
options.D: Finish internal cylindrical surfaces, such as cylinder bores, to a fine surface finish and close limits with abrasive stones

e: Honing is carried out to finish internal cylindrical surfaces, such as cylinder bores, to a fine surface finish and close limits with abrasive stones.

q: 'Knurling' on a lathe is the operation of:

options.A: Cutting a helical groove on a cylindrical surface
options.B: Producing a roughened (diamond or straight) pattern on a cylindrical surface so as to provide a better grip
options.C: Reducing the diameter of a workpiece by a forming tool
options.D: Facing the end of a workpiece square to its axis

e: Knurling is the operation of producing a roughened (diamond or straight) pattern on a cylindrical surface so as to provide a better grip.

q: The lead screw of a centre lathe is used primarily for:

options.A: Cutting screw threads on the workpiece by driving the carriage at a precise ratio to the spindle rotation
options.B: Providing the ordinary longitudinal feed for turning operations
options.D: Driving the tailstock along the bed of the lathe

e: The lead screw of a centre lathe drives the carriage at a precise ratio to the spindle rotation, which is what makes accurate screw thread cutting possible.

q: In connection with modern machine tools in workshops, the abbreviation CNC stands for:
e: In connection with modern machine tools, CNC stands for Computer Numerical Control.

q: Spot welding, as used in the building of coach bodies in a workshop, is:

options.A: A form of arc welding done with a coated electrode
options.B: A form of resistance welding in which overlapping sheet-metal parts are joined at localised points by heat generated by electric resistance under pressure
options.C: A gas welding process using a carburising flame
options.D: A process of joining metals with a low-melting-point alloy

e: Spot welding is a form of resistance welding in which overlapping sheet-metal parts are joined at localised points by heat generated by electric resistance under pressure.

q: MIG welding, used in workshops, is a process of:

options.A: Arc welding in which a continuously fed consumable wire electrode is used and the weld is shielded by an inert gas
options.B: Welding in which the joint is heated by a thermit reaction
options.C: Resistance welding of rails in situ
options.D: Welding carried out under water with a special electrode

e: MIG welding is arc welding in which a continuously fed consumable wire electrode is used and the weld is shielded by an inert gas.

q: In die casting, components are produced by:

options.A: Pouring molten metal into a sand mould by gravity
options.B: Hammering heated metal into shape between dies
options.C: Forcing molten metal under high pressure into a permanent steel mould (die), giving accurate parts in large numbers
options.D: Spinning a mould so that the metal is thrown against its walls

e: In die casting, molten metal is forced under high pressure into a permanent steel mould (die), giving accurate parts in large numbers.

q: In the Brinell hardness test carried out on workshop materials, the hardness is determined by:

options.A: Scratching the surface with a diamond point
options.B: Measuring the rebound of a dropped hammer
options.C: Filing the surface and comparing the marks with a standard
options.D: Pressing a hardened steel ball into the surface under a standard load and measuring the diameter of the indentation

e: In the Brinell hardness test, a hardened steel ball is pressed into the surface under a standard load and the diameter of the indentation is measured to determine the hardness.

q: In a railway workshop, the abbreviation EOT crane stands for:
e: In a railway workshop, EOT crane stands for Electric Overhead Travelling crane.

q: A 'traverser' provided in a workshop or yard serves the purpose of:

options.A: Lifting a coach body clear of its bogies
options.C: Transferring rolling stock or vehicles sideways from one track to another parallel track

e: A traverser serves the purpose of transferring rolling stock or vehicles sideways from one track to another parallel track.

q: Freight wagons of Indian Railways, such as the BOXN type, are fitted with bogies of the design known as:
e: Freight wagons of Indian Railways, such as the BOXN type, are fitted with bogies of the CASNUB design.

q: The Wheel Slide Protection (WSP) device fitted on LHB coaches serves to:

options.A: Protect the wheels against theft while standing in the yard
options.B: Indicate the speed of the coach to the driver
options.C: Lubricate the wheel flanges on curves
options.D: Prevent skidding of wheels and formation of wheel flats during heavy braking

e: The Wheel Slide Protection (WSP) device fitted on LHB coaches prevents skidding of wheels and the formation of wheel flats during heavy braking.

q: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) is located at Chittaranjan in the State of:
e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW) is located at Chittaranjan in the State of West Bengal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In nitriding, the surface of a steel component is hardened by the diffusion of nitrogen into it, forming a hard layer of nitrides.
2. In induction hardening, only the surface layer of a component is heated rapidly by a high-frequency electric current and then quenched.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: in nitriding the surface is hardened by diffusion of nitrogen forming hard nitrides, and in induction hardening only the surface layer is heated rapidly by a high-frequency current and then quenched.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The dye penetrant test is used to detect surface-breaking defects in a component and can be applied to non-magnetic materials also.
2. Radiographic (X-ray/gamma ray) testing is used to reveal internal defects in castings and welded joints.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the dye penetrant test detects surface-breaking defects and can be applied to non-magnetic materials also, while radiographic testing reveals internal defects in castings and welded joints.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A trade union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 is a body corporate, having perpetual succession and a common seal.
2. Registration of a trade union is compulsory under the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: a registered trade union is a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal. Statement 2 is wrong, as registration of a trade union under the Act is not compulsory.
